subject: Backup erasure propagation, proof and timeline request
messages:
From: Sara Malik <sara@fintegrity.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@fintegrity.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Backup erasure propagation & audit evidence request

Hi Jonas,

We're preparing for an upcoming compliance review and need clarifications on how Redwood handles backup deletion/expunge propagation across regions and what evidence you can provide. Specific questions from our legal/compliance teams: 

- If a user in our account requests deletion (and the primary dataset is removed), what is the typical timeline until the corresponding backup snapshots are hard-expunged (fully removed from all replicas)? Please include regional variance (us-west, us-east, eu-west).
- What markers do you use to indicate "tombstone" vs "hard-expunge" and where are those reflected in audit logs?
- How does a legal hold / litigation hold interact with your backup expunge workflow? If we place a hold, is expunge prevented indefinitely or is there a maximum preservation override?
- For our SOC/PCI auditors we need: a sample audit export showing a deletion request, snapshot ID(s), expunge events, and KMS key operations tied to the expunge. Can you provide a redacted example?

I've attached our retention checklist (FC-Data-Retention-Checklist.pdf) for context. We prefer a written response we can share with auditors and a tentative date for when Redwood can deliver the evidence exports.

Thanks,
Sara Malik
Head of Security
Fintegrity Payments

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sara Malik <sara@fintegrity.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Backup erasure propagation & audit evidence request

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik and Marissa (security & product) to add implementation detail and evidence artifacts. High level answers below; Karthik will follow up with the event-level timeline and sample exports.

Summary (short):
- Tombstone vs hard-expunge: We use a two‑phase model. A delete request creates a tombstone marker immediately and prevents normal reads; backups keep tombstones and data until the expunge window completes. Hard-expunge (irreversible removal of shard blobs and associated KV) is an asynchronous job that runs per-region.
- Typical timing: primary-delete -> tombstone (seconds). Hard-expunge completion varies by policy and region; default scheduled expunge job runs in a weekly window but is configurable for enterprise customers. Typical default: 7–30 days to hard-expunge across all replicas.
- Legal hold: placing a retention/hold suspends expunge for the hold scope. Holds are retained until explicitly released; we do not auto-drop holds. There are administrative controls — if you need indefinite preservation we can document and apply a retention override for your account.
- Evidence exports: we can provide a bundled export that includes the deletion request id, snapshot manifest(s), expunge job events, and the KMS envelope events. We will redact account-sensitive tokens but preserve timestamps, snapshot IDs, and event hashes for auditor verification.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Karthik will produce a sample export (redacted) and an expunge timeline matrix for us-west/us-east/eu-west.
2) We provide a 2‑page attestation describing the retention + hold behavior and controls.
3) If you want a signed attestation/DocuSign, we can route through legal and estimate delivery in 7 business days from confirmation.

If you need an accelerated expunge or an on-demand proof run for a single object, tell us the object id and we can perform an isolated audit run (may require elevated ops windows).

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Malik <sara@fintegrity.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Backup erasure propagation & audit evidence request

Sara — adding the technical runbook and a small matrix for expectations. Quoting Jonas below for context.

On 2026-05-17 12:02, Jonas Weber wrote:
> Summary (short):
> - Tombstone vs hard-expunge: We use a two‑phase model...

Technical detail and evidence we will provide:
- Expunge flow: 1) Delete request created -> tombstone flag applied to primary object metadata. 2) Background snapshot process captures tombstone state in the next backup cycle (delta snapshots). 3) Expunge scheduler marks candidate objects for irreversible removal and enqueues per-region expunge workers. 4) Workers delete object blobs and emit "expunge.completed" events to the audit stream.
- Per-region timing (default config): us-west: 7–14 days; us-east: 7–21 days; eu-west: 10–30 days. These windows cover replication throttles and offsite archival retention policies.
- Holds: Scoped holds set a retention flag on object(s) and block expunge.jobs. Holds are indefinite until removed; they do not auto-expire. We will attach the API call and the admin UI steps for applying/removing holds.
- Audit artifacts we'll include (redacted): deletion_request.json (request_id, user, timestamp), snapshot_manifest.csv (snapshot_id, region, object_ids), audit_events.log (expunge.scheduled, expunge.started, expunge.completed), kms_key_ops.log (Encrypt/Decrypt/KeyDelete events).

Notes and caveats:
- If you use cross-region replication with an immutable offsite archive (customer-configured S3 with retention lock), Redwood's expunge job will mark the object as expunged internally but cannot delete third-party immutable archives; you'll need to coordinate deletion at the archive owner.
- For forensic proof we provide event hashes and signatures tied to the expunge.completed event so auditors can verify non-repudiation without exposing raw payloads.

Mutual Action Plan (suggested):
- Today +1: Confirm number of sample events required and the account(s) to redact.
- +3 business days: We deliver redacted export and the per-region expunge matrix (CSV).
- +7 business days: Deliver 2‑page attestation; legal can sign DocuSign if requested.

Attachment: sample-expunge-manifest.csv (contains synthetic snapshot IDs and event timelines for auditor review).

If you want, we can also run a time‑boxed evidence extraction against a demo tenant and share raw event dumps under an NDA.

—Karthik
Principal Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
